newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - BHP still mulling Dai Hung options.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - BHP still mulling Dai Hung options.

text.p: Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Wednesday that it was still weighing its options over its 43.75 percent stake in Dai Hung oil project in Vietnam.
BHP is the operator of the project.

Malaysia's state-run oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) said on Monday it is prepared to take over as operator of Dai Hung oil from BHP's unit BHP Petroleum, if all parties in the project agreed to the move.
BHP Petroleum spokesman Robert Porter told Reuters that BHP had held a number of talks over the possible sale of its Dai Hung stake, but no sale to Petronas had been formed.
"We have been looking at a number of options," Porter said.
Porter said BHP was still in discussions with the Vietnamese government over its future role in the project.

The Dai Hung field, once thought to be one of Asia's largest, is owned by a consortium comprising BHP with a 43.75 percent stake, Petronas with 20 percent, Vietnam's state-owned PetroVietnam with 15 percent and Total Sa and Sumitomo Corp with 10.625 percent each.
BHP said in September it would be interested in any reasonable offer for its stake in Dai Hung.

The company, which fully wrote down its A$151 million Dai Hung investment in its 1995/96 accounts, had been trying to renegotiate terms of its contract with PetroVietnam after estimates of the field's reserves were slashed.
According to initial estimates, Dai Hung had recoverable oil reserves of 700 million barrels but this was later revised downwards to 100 million barrels.
